product.title: landmark points per tile (schools, hospitals, airports, churches held, fire stations, parks)

standing.claim: Fetch.file stores each downloaded body (line 772) before the caller checks it, so an error page or error JSON that arrives with HTTP 200 becomes the cached copy and is re-read on every later run until a --refresh.
standing.evidence: Reproduced on a copy of the builder's cache (drv/repro_failures.py, case A): run 1 with one HTTP 200 error body leaves the PAD-US parks unavailable and the cached page holds the error text; run 2 with a healthy server makes 0 requests and the parks stay unavailable. The integration notes save the p3-cache folder between daily runs, so the failure lasts until the monthly refresh. Callers that trust the stored body: lines 808, 825, 852-853 and 873.
standing.fix: Validate before the write: pass a check into Fetch.file (a JSON object without an 'error' member, a zip holding APT.txt, the shapefile parts) and write to the cache only after it passes; a failed check writes nothing and raises SourceFailure. Add a test that an error body sent with HTTP 200 is not cached and that the next run requests it again.

standing.claim: An unavailable kind reports a count of 0 in counts.kinds, and map_data_landmarks passes that zero on to map.json. Rule 5 forbids a zero for a missing input.
standing.evidence: Reproduced (case C): with the FAA file missing, state is partial, kinds.airport.state is unavailable, counts.kinds.airport is 0, and map.json counts.kinds.airport is 0. The zero comes from line 1091 (count=0 for unavailable kinds). Line 1130 gives held rows 0 when the FEMA source failed, and line 1176 writes points 0 for mark_unavailable. Integration notes section 4 mirrors these counts into hail/index.json.
standing.fix: Write null, not 0, for the count of a kind that did not load, for points and shards in an unavailable block, and for held rows when the held source failed. Drop the counts of unavailable kinds in map_data_landmarks (line 1217). Add a test that an unavailable kind's count is null in the index and in map.json.

standing.claim: BuildTests needs the park source to load, so it fails when pyshp is absent. Only the TIGER tests skip, which breaks the brief's skip rule and the repository convention.
standing.evidence: Run with sys.modules['shapefile'] = None: 43 tests, 1 failure (test_the_build_writes_the_shards_the_block_and_the_manifest at line 374: 'partial' != 'loaded'), 2 skipped. tests/test_basemap2.py gates its pyshp tests with skipUnless (lines 205 and 262). .github/workflows/check-app.yml runs on every pull_request and runs python -m unittest discover -s tests after installing only flask, folium, requests, waitress, tzdata, pillow and numpy, so it would fail there.
standing.fix: Decorate BuildTests with @unittest.skipUnless(HAVE_SHAPEFILE, 'pyshp is not installed'), or, when pyshp is missing, assert state 'partial' and that the parks are unavailable.

standing.claim: The full suite is red. test_landmarks.py is in neither on.push.paths (lines 25-50) nor the offline unittest line (line 115), and four other B6 modules have the same gap. The P3 integration notes do not ask for this workflow edit.
standing.evidence: Whole suite on a copy of the worktree: Ran 2199 tests in 405.7 s, FAILED (failures=6, skipped=12). The six failures are test_website_workflow.PushPathsCoverTheTests: push-path failures for test_basemap2, test_history_layers, test_labels, test_landmarks and test_terrain, and the offline-line failure naming the same five. The builder's own logs/full-suite.log (20:56) shows the same pins. The contract is in tests/test_website_workflow.py lines 202-218.
standing.fix: Add tests/test_landmarks.py, tests/test_terrain.py, tests/test_basemap2.py, tests/test_history_layers.py and tests/test_labels.py to website.yml on.push.paths and to the offline unittest line (115). Put this step in integration.md, since it is the integrator's phase B work, and do not merge until the suite is green.

standing.claim: D16 says a source that cannot be read fails only that source, but run() catches only SourceFailure. Any other exception ends build(), so every kind is lost and no per-source reason is recorded.
standing.evidence: Reproduced (case B): setting the NCES public layer's maxRecordCount to 'many' makes build() raise ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'many'. The same can happen at line 816 with other malformed metadata. The pyshp record loop (lines 686-688) is outside the try block in read_tiger, so a damaged DBF can raise a pyshp error that escapes the same way.
standing.fix: In run(), catch Exception as well, record it as a SourceFailure with its plain reason and print it. Wrap the pyshp record loop and the metadata parse in SourceFailure. Add a test with a malformed layer description: the other sources still load and only that kind is unavailable.

standing.claim: Two rights sentences are attributed to the layers ('The layer says') but neither appears in the layer data the build reads.
standing.evidence: The cached layer descriptions (/home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/cache/P3/padus_local/meta.json and fema_worship/meta.json) and the live service roots fetched on 2026-10-25 contain no 'public domain' text for PAD-US (its copyrightText is the USGS GAP 2025 citation with DOI 10.5066/P96WBCHS) and no 'limitation' text for the FEMA layer (its copyrightText says the points were geocoded by a commercial geocoder). The docstring (line 32), the padus_local terms (lines 192-193), the fema_worship terms (lines 211-212) and integration notes section 1 (padus_local 'missing') repeat the unsupported sentences.
standing.fix: Quote only what the layer states: for PAD-US, its copyright citation and DOI; for FEMA, 'The layer's copyright line says the points were geocoded by a commercial geocoder whose terms are not read.' If a public-domain statement exists on the USGS item page, cite that page and its date. Counsel should see the exact text.

standing.claim: The CONTRACTS rows do not match the module's sources, the About lines are not verbatim, and the roadmap line miscounts the sources.
standing.evidence: The rows use 'nces_schools', which is not a module key, and omit hifld_hospitals. The module defines nces_public, nces_private, usgs_hospitals, hifld_hospitals, faa_nasr, usgs_fire, padus_local, tiger_park and fema_worship (landmarks.py lines 133-214). Section 7 (line 169) says the credit lines are verbatim from SOURCES, but the hospital, airport and park lines differ from the SOURCES credits (lines 155, 173, 191, 199). Section 8 (line 182) says 'five public lists'; the module reads seven source files. The brief requires one CONTRACTS row per source.
standing.fix: Write nine rows keyed by the module's keys. Copy the About lines from describe_landmarks() output, or drop the word 'verbatim'. Say 'seven public source files' or name them.

standing.claim: The P3 output folder has no report.md, although the brief lists it among the outputs (report.md, integration.md, measurements.json, logs).
standing.evidence: /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/build/P3/ holds integration.md, measurements.json, logs/ and store/. A search of /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6 finds no P3 report.
standing.fix: Write report.md: what was built, the checks and their results, the budgets, the statewide counts, and the owner's open items (the held church kind, the Rose Garden name, the hospital source, the FAA cycle date).

standing.claim: The committed FAA sample holds owner names, mailing addresses, phone numbers and manager names of private owners, in a public repository, although the module's own rule keeps contact data out of its output.
standing.evidence: Line 1: owner PETTY CREEK MOUNTAIN RANCH LLC, its address, phone 406-370-1915, manager WAYNE WILLIAMS. Line 3: owner ROBERT & CHERYLL SMITH, BOX 58, ULM, MT, phone 406-866-3328, manager ROBERT D SMITH. Line 2: manager RORY DERENBURGER. The module keeps none of these fields (docstring lines 5-6), and the repository is public.
standing.fix: Blank the owner, address, phone and manager columns (layout columns 188 to 523) in the fixture. The parser reads only columns 15-27, 49-50, 134-183, 186-187, 524-565 and 841-842. Re-run the FAA tests.

standing.claim: The notes say the monthly job asks again for every file, but give no monthly command. Without --refresh the cache is never refreshed, so the layers would stay as first fetched.
standing.evidence: The module's help text says --refresh is for the monthly job (landmarks.py line 1356). Without it Fetch.file reads every cached file (line 765), so the daily command in section 6 never re-requests anything it has cached.
standing.fix: Write the monthly command with --refresh and the same --cache folder in the notes and in the monthly job of hail-store.yml.

standing.claim: Displayed names keep source abbreviations and odd capitals.
standing.evidence: Built airport names include 'Condon Usfs Airport', 'Schafer /Usfs/ Airport', 'Wokal Fld/Glasgow-Valley County Airport', 'Woltermann Meml Airport' and 'Big Timber At Howard Field'. School names include '227 Academy- Hs' and '12Th St W Park'. AIRPORT_WORDS (line 327) lacks MEML, and the whole-word rule at line 347 misses FLD inside a token. Title-casing comes from stations.display_name (line 340).
standing.fix: Owner decision on the display rule. At least expand MEML, split FLD from a slash token, keep USFS as an acronym, and keep 'at' lower case.

standing.claim: The as-of text for the two USGS layers is a constant, not read from the service. The build never requests the service copyright line.
standing.evidence: Lines 154 and 180 hard-code 'October 2026 refresh (service copyright line)'. The live MapServer root reads 'USGS TNM - National Structures Dataset. Data Refreshed October, 2026.' today, so the text is true now but will not update.
standing.fix: Read the MapServer root's copyrightText (one cached request), or write the constant as 'as written in SOURCES on 2026-10-25'.

standing.claim: About strings repeat years and nest parentheses, and the FAA credit ends with a pointer to the About page.
standing.evidence: Output: 'NCES EDGE public school locations, 2024-25 (2024-25 school year).'; 'USGS The National Map, hospitals and medical centers (October 2026 refresh (service copyright line)).'; the FAA credit (line 173) ends 'the cycle named in About.'. The formats are at line 234 (source_item) and lines 1192-1193.
standing.fix: Write the as-of without a second parenthesis, drop the repeated year, and give the FAA credit the cycle date itself (for example 'for the 2026-10-01 cycle').

standing.claim: When the HIFLD fallback fails, the hospital kind names usgs_hospitals as the failed source, although that source loaded.
standing.evidence: Line 1084 sets failed to ['usgs_hospitals'] whenever hospital_key is None, so the index names the wrong source and the kind's sources list is empty. The HIFLD failure is recorded separately in failures.
standing.fix: Name hifld_hospitals as the failed source in that branch and keep the USGS reason in the block.

standing.claim: The test file contains a literal em dash inside its own assertion, against the repository rule.
standing.evidence: grep finds one em dash character on line 537 (self.assertNotIn with the dash character as its first argument).
standing.fix: Write the character as a Python escape (backslash u 2014) in the test.

standing.claim: Several failure paths have no test. The verify command is not tested to fail, load_faa's non-zip and missing-APT.txt paths (landmarks.py lines 853-865) are not tested, and the command-line exit codes (lines 1367-1396) are not tested.
standing.evidence: I tampered a copy of a built store (one row added, manifest and counts unchanged): verify returned ok false with six failed checks, so the function works, but nothing in the suite pins it.
standing.fix: Add three small tests: verify fails on a tampered shard; a non-zip FAA file and a zip without APT.txt are unavailable; main() returns 1 on a missing store and 0 on a build.

standing.claim: The FAA zip cache is never pruned. Each cycle is about 9.9 MB and there are 13 cycles a year, against a 1 GB per-product budget in the brief.
standing.evidence: Path construction at line 851 keys each cycle by name; no code deletes older APT_*.zip files.
standing.fix: After a successful build, delete the other APT_*.zip files in the cache folder.

standing.claim: The label point is the pole of inaccessibility measured in degrees, so longitude is not scaled by cos(latitude) and the pole is not the metric centre. The docstring says the point is computed to about 1 metre, which is true of the 1e-5 degree precision but not of the distance measure.
standing.evidence: The search runs in lon/lat degrees (pole_of_inaccessibility, lines 414-461). Every label point lies inside its polygon (554 of 554 checked), so there is no containment error.
standing.fix: Scale longitude by cos(mean latitude) before the search, or state in the docstring that the distance is in degrees.

standing.claim: The store docstring's kind code list omits 'c' (church, held and never written).
standing.evidence: Line 56 lists s, h, a, f and p only; KIND_CODE (line 123) includes c.
standing.fix: Add 'c church (held; never written)' to the list.

standing.claim: The HIFLD terms text says 'not confirmed', which the shared forbidden-word list flags. The field is internal and is not shown on the page.
standing.evidence: Shared-list scan of all 39 user-facing and source strings: only hifld_hospitals.terms (line 167) is flagged ('confirmed').
standing.fix: Write 'not checked' in the terms text.
